description:
Takımımız; Yapay Zeka (Bilgisayarlı Görü, RAG, LLM) ve modern Web teknolojilerini kullanarak yenilikçi çözümler üretmek amacıyla kurulmuştur.

Bu yılki NASA Space Apps Challenge'da "Flame in Freefall" görevi üzerinde çalışıyoruz. Amacımız, mikro yerçekimi ortamındaki veri setlerini kullanarak uzay misyonları için yapay zeka destekli bir yangın güvenliği analizi projesi geliştirmek.

Tam donanımlı bir ürün ortaya koyabilmek ve dereceye oynamak için ekibimizi tamamlayacak şu alanlarda takım arkadaşları arıyoruz

AI/ML, Veri Analizi, Tasarım (UI/UX & Grafik), Web Geliştirme (Frontend), Hikayeleştirme ve Sunum (Storytelling)

Uzay teknolojilerine ve inovasyona ilgi duyan herkesi takımımıza bekliyoruz!
summary: Flame in Freefall is a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion research into fire safety insight for crews heading to the Moon and Mars. Decades of experiments are public in NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database, but the details are scattered across reports, pages and data files, and every experiment uses different fuels, hardware and conditions. We collected 19 investigations into one verified, source-cited format so they can be searched, filtered and compared side by side. An atmosphere chart shows where each test sits relative to Earth, spacesuit and planned lunar base conditions, a relevance ranking explains which investigations matter most for a lunar base, rover or station, and an SI assistant answers questions using only these records and cites the investigation behind every claim. This matters because a planned lunar base atmosphere has an oxygen fraction more than 40% higher than Earth air, so materials burn much more easily, while almost no data exists at lunar or Martian gravity. We show those gaps openly instead of hiding them.
details: WHAT IT DOES Flame in Freefall brings 19 NASA microgravity combustion investigations into one dashboard. Investigation cards show every experiment in the same format: goal, fuel, conditions, sensors, hardware, key result and source. Compare puts 2 to 4 investigations side by side and separates shared fields from differing ones. The atmosphere chart plots every test point by oxygen fraction and pressure, with Earth air, spacesuit and planned lunar base / pressurized rover zones marked. Habitat relevance gives a score for lunar base, rover and station, with the reasons behind it. Nearest experiments ("What if?") lets you set oxygen, pressure, temperature and airflow and see which investigations ran closest to those conditions. Safety pillars group the work by prevention, detection and suppression. Data gaps lists 65 documented gaps, including the lack of measurements at lunar and Martian gravity. The SI assistant and smart filter answer plain-language questions. Everything can be exported as CSV, JSON or PDF, in English and Turkish (EN / TR button at the top right). HOW IT WORKS Each investigation was read from NASA PSI and other NASA sources and written into a single shared schema. Every field keeps its source and a supporting sentence (264 evidence citations in total). Our rule: nothing is written without a source, and unknown fields stay empty. All 19 records are verified. The SI layer is deliberately constrained. The assistant receives all investigation records and must answer from them alone; every claim carries an investigation ID that is checked against real records, and if the answer is not in the data it says so. In the smart filter the model only judges how well each criterion is met and must point to the supporting field; the 0-10 score is computed by code and its breakdown is shown to the user. If the primary model fails, a fallback model takes over; if none works, a prepared answer is returned instead of an invented one. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Mission planners, engineers, students and researchers can find, compare and interpret microgravity fire experiments in minutes instead of reading scattered reports. They can see at a glance which results apply to lunar habitat conditions, where oxygen is more than 40% higher than in Earth air, and where data is still missing, so future experiments can target those gaps. WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE We treat honesty about data as a feature: gaps are shown, not hidden, and SI is never allowed to produce a number or a claim without a traceable source. TOOLS Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, i18next, hosted on Vercel. Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, jsonschema, fpdf2 (PDF export), hosted on Render. SI: Google Gemini through the google-genai SDK with a fallback model chain. Data: JSON files with a shared schema, 12 automated tests, schema validation, rate limiting and CORS protection.
